extracted.intended_audience: IP office statisticians, policymakers, researchers, and patent/design professionals who analyze industrial design application and registration statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and interpreting WIPO industrial design statistical metrics and procedural indicators (application counts, registrations, office performance and normalization by GDP/population) for cross-office and cross‑country comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application design counts (absolute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application design counts are based on the numbers of applications filed (absolute count, not equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note states: 'Data are based on the numbers of applications filed; this means that differences between single-design and multiple-design filing systems across IP offices are not taken into account.' Used in figures/tables for offices and origins (top offices, selected low- and middle-income offices/origins). Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent application design counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent application design counts convert regional filings to counts equivalent to multiple applications in member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The origin of an industrial design application is determined by the residence of the first named applicant. 'Applications filed at some regional offices are considered equivalent to multiple applications in the member states of those offices. See glossary for the definition of equivalent application and design count.' Used for 'equivalent' counts by origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration design counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of industrial design registrations (registrations issued by offices) by office and origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures/tables show registration design counts for offices (top 20, selected low- and middle-income offices). Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023. Footnotes clarify when only Hague designation data are available or origin data are incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution of resident and non-resident counts to total growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of total growth in application/registration design counts into contributions from resident and non-resident applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure shows total growth broken down by contributions of resident and non-resident applicants, with example: 'total design counts in the US decreased by 5.5%, with resident applicants contributing 3.3 percentage points to the overall decline and non-resident applicants 2.2 percentage points.' Applicable to offices and selected origins (2021–2022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident application design counts by filing route
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of non-resident applications broken down by filing route (e.g., national filing, Hague System, regional routes) over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in time-series figure (2008–2022). Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023. Useful to identify how non-resident filings reach an office (direct, via Hague, regional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application design counts by origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Application design counts attributed to origins (residence of first named applicant) for top origins and selected low-/middle-income origins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: 'The origin of an industrial design application is determined by the residence of the first named applicant. An application filed at a regional office is considered to be a resident filing, if the applicant resides in one of that office’s member states.' Data may be absolute or equivalent as indicated in captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application design counts by Locarno class
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of applications categorized by Locarno classification (top Locarno classes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure C22 covers top 10 Locarno classes for 2022 (based on data from 115 IP offices). Annex C provides class numbers. Data for some large offices may be missing or incomplete (e.g., Japan, US).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application design counts by industry sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of design applications aggregated into industry sectors using an OECD concordance (32 Locarno classes converted into 12 industry sectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in figure C23 and distribution breakdowns. See annex C for definitions. Based on data from 115 IP offices; some large offices' data may be incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of application design counts by top sectors (by office/origin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share/distribution of application counts across the top three industry sectors for selected offices or origins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures C24 and C25 show distribution for top 10 offices and top 10 origins respectively, selected based on 2022 totals. Based on OECD concordance and data availability caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident application design count per USD 100 billion of GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalization of resident application counts by economic output: number of resident design applications per USD 100 billion of GDP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure C26 uses GDP in constant 2017 US PPP dollars and selects origins based on application counts and GDP data availability. Sources: WIPO Statistics Database and World Bank, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident application design count per million population
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident application design counts normalized per million population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure C27 compares top 20 origins for 2012 and 2022; origins selected based on application design count and population data availability. Sources: WIPO Statistics Database and World Bank, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident application design count per capita vs GDP per capita (relationship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison/relationship between resident application design count per capita and GDP per capita over time for selected origins (2018–2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure C28 presents selected origins from different world regions and income groups. Useful to analyze correlation between design activity and economic well‑being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design registrations in force (trend and totals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of industrial design registrations in force (stock), aggregated worldwide and by office; refers to registrations in force, not number of designs within registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO estimates cover 136 IP offices and include direct national/regional applications and Hague designations. Data refer to the number of registrations in force, not the number of designs contained in those registrations. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations in force as percentage of total registrations (by registration year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages calculated as number of industrial designs registered in year t and in force in 2022 divided by total number registered in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure C31 is based on data from 90 offices for which breakdown by year of registration was available. Notes: industrial design rights generally last up to 15 years from filing; China limited to 10 years and was excluded from this figure because it accounts for most of the global total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of industrial design registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Average age (years) of registrations in force at selected offices (comparison years e.g., 2017 and 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentages in the related figure are calculated using the number of industrial designs registered in year t and in force in 2022 divided by the total number registered in year t. Source: WIPO Statistics Database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of industrial design examination outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of examination outcomes (e.g., registered, rejected, withdrawn/abandoned, pending) for selected offices in a given year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure C33 shows distribution for selected offices (2022). WIPO notes that data are collected via a common questionnaire, but differences in industrial design procedures between offices limit full harmonization—exercise caution when comparing offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potentially pending applications (pending backlog measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count/measure of potentially pending applications at selected offices for a given year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure C34 presents 'potentially pending applications' for selected offices (2022). WIPO cautions differences in procedures and missing data for some large offices (e.g., China, Italy, Japan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average pendency times (first office action and final decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number of days from filing date to first office action and from filing date to final office decision for selected offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure C35 provides average pendency times for 2022. WIPO collects data via a common questionnaire but cautions about differences in procedures across offices that prevent full harmonization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of industrial design examiners (FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of industrial design examiners expressed in full‑time equivalents (FTE) for selected offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure C36 and the procedural table list examiners (FTE) for selected offices (2022). This metric is used alongside pendency and throughput measures to assess office capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design office procedural data (per-office throughput and disposition categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per-office table entries including Total applications processed; Registered; Rejected; Withdrawn or abandoned; Applications pending; Number of examiners (FTE); First office action from filing date (days); Final office decision from filing date (days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table C39 (procedural data, 2022) provides these columns for many offices. Used to measure office performance and workload. WIPO notes data collection via a common questionnaire but cautions that different procedures across offices mean data cannot be fully harmonized and some large offices' data are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data completeness, coverage and harmonization caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements about incomplete or missing data, differences in national/regional procedures, and limits to comparability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple notes: e.g., 'Data for several of the larger offices are either not available or incomplete, including for the offices of Japan and the US.'; 'WIPO collects data from offices using a common questionnaire and methodology. However, because of differences in industrial design procedures between offices, data cannot be fully harmonized. Therefore, caution should be exercised when making comparisons across offices.' Footnotes (a,b,c,d), 'n.a.' and '..' indicate not applicable/not available. Use these caveats when interpreting and comparing series.
